_doc: Post-promote guard for the web_design_v2 blueprint (brand_extract → design → verify → assemble). This is the ONLY scenario exercising the computed-assembly, interactive, verified web-design path: the `design` stage calls html_render_service in mode=assembly, whose internal render + JS-console + axe-a11y verify/refine lane mark_fails a broken design — which raises the design stage and prevents the run from completing. So a terminal `completed` here PROVES a verified interactive design was produced end-to-end; `verify` re-asserts the report is not failing (defense-in-depth) and `assemble` emits the live artifact URLs. Brand is supplied INLINE (project `brand` block) so the nightly guard has no hard dependency on analysis_service's brand-from-url fetch (brand_extract is best-effort and never fails the run). No `embeds`: the three.js seam needs a real fetchable artifact URL from the future embed service, so it is validated separately once that exists — not in this guard. brief.description is REQUIRED (the design stage raises StageError without it). pause_after_stages:[] runs straight to `completed` through design→verify→assemble. expect_stage_assertions on `assemble` prove the artifact surfaced (live_html_url + redesign_job_id) and that verification ran (verification_status) — a green terminal alone would not catch a regression that completes without a verified, fetchable design. deadline/timeout in the workflow matrix are widened for the design stage's LLM plan + Chromium render + up to 2 refine passes (~3000s worst case).

brief.description: A clean single-page marketing landing page for a developer-tools startup, with a hero, a feature grid, social-proof logos, pricing, an FAQ, and a single primary call-to-action.
brief.audience: engineering leads evaluating a developer tool

_checks_doc: STRENGTHENED 2026-09-05. Two assertions here could not fail. (1) `nonempty verification_status` PASSES on the literal string "failed" — nonempty only tests that the resolved value is a non-blank str (e2e_validate.py::_eval_check). The real success literal is "passed": web_design_v2/verify.py raises StageError unless the design's status is "passed" (or the absent "skipped"/None case, which itself raises while `web_design_require_verification` is ON — the default), and assemble.py:56 sets verification_status = verify.get("status") or design.get("verification_status"), where VerifyOutput.status is that same literal. So `equals "passed"` is what this scenario always meant, and it adds no NEW red risk under the default setting: any non-passed status already fails the verify stage and therefore the run. (2) `nonempty live_html_url` is near-vacuous by construction — assemble.py:54 falls back to f"/api/redesign/jobs/{job_id}/html", so it is non-empty whenever a job id exists (which the line above it already requires). It is kept (cheap) but no longer carries the spec. The new load-bearing check is the rendered artifact: `visuals[].image_url`, collected at design.py:165 (_collect_visuals) from the `generate_screenshots=True, screenshot_viewports=["desktop"]` submit — a Chromium screenshot OF the assembled page. RedesignVisual.image_url is a required str (website_review/redesign.py:88) and website_review_variants_happy_path asserts this same path live. The `verify` stage assertion is new too: it names the gate stage explicitly so a verify that silently stops running is a NAMED failure rather than a missing one.
